ui.alert.title: {name}!
ui.alert.body.fire: The city is on fire. Flames spread to neighbouring tiles and only a road, water or a bulldozed firebreak will stop them. Fire brigades help only where they reach.
ui.alert.body.wildfire: The forest is burning. There is time to cut a break before the fire reaches the buildings — after that it is too late.
ui.alert.body.flood: Water is rising and flooding the lowland. Flooded buildings decay until it recedes. A raised bank holds it back.
ui.alert.body.tornado: A tornado is crossing the city, taking whatever stands in its way. It cannot be stopped, only cleaned up after.
ui.alert.body.earthquake: An earthquake. Buildings collapse or drop a level, roads and pipes crack. Tall blocks take it better than low ones.
ui.alert.body.explosion: An explosion. The surroundings are flattened and burning.
ui.alert.body.industrialAccident: An industrial accident. Blast and fire have hit the surrounding area.
ui.alert.body.pileup: A pile-up is blocking the road. Traffic around it is stuck until it is cleared.
ui.alert.body.strike: A strike in the district. Services there are down and happiness falls until conditions improve. An unresolved strike can grow into a riot.
ui.alert.body.riot: Civil unrest. The district is out of control, land value is falling and the police have their hands full.
ui.alert.body.gangWar: A gang war. Nothing is destroyed, but the district gets permanently worse — crime up, land value down.
ui.alert.body.blackout: A blackout. Power plants have dropped out and without power the services are down too, so the risk of everything else has jumped.
ui.alert.body.epidemic: An epidemic. Disease is spreading among the residents and people are dying. Only enough health coverage will stop it.
ui.alert.body.chemicalSpill: A chemical spill. The waterworks is out and the surroundings stay poisoned even after the leak ends.
ui.alert.body.landslide: A landslide. The slope gave way and took what stood on it.

ui.alert.story.fire:
Fire. Flames have broken through the windows into the street and smoke is creeping under the neighbours’ doors. The brigade is on its way, but until it arrives the fire spreads — and what burns is not repaired, it is demolished.

Check whether that quarter has a fire station within reach at all.
ui.alert.story.wildfire:
The woods are burning. Wind is driving the fire up the slope and embers are landing where we expected quiet. The smoke is visible across the whole city.

Until the flames reach bare ground or water, they will not stop on their own.
ui.alert.story.flood:
The water has risen. Low streets are under the surface, ground floors are filling and nothing gets through. The drains cannot cope.

When it falls there will be mud, mould and a bill. Building on the flood plain was always a bet.
ui.alert.story.tornado:
A tornado came through. In a few minutes it took roofs, snapped trees and left a strip you can see from the far side of town.

What stood in its way no longer stands. The rest was lucky.
ui.alert.story.earthquake:
The whole city shook. The asphalt has cracked, balconies came off the facades and people are standing outside looking at their houses.

Older buildings may not have taken it. Someone will have to count what can be saved.
ui.alert.story.explosion:
An explosion. The ground floor is gone, there is a hole where a wall was and glass reached across the street. They heard it in the next quarter.

Everything within the radius took it head on. The rest took a fright.
ui.alert.story.industrialAccident:
An accident at the works. The hall roof is open, steam is escaping from the pipework and what used to be a tank is lying in the yard.

Production has stopped and the neighbourhood pays in health and in land value. Industry next to housing always has this catch.
ui.alert.story.pileup:
A pile-up. Vehicles are blocking both lanes and traffic around it is at a standstill. Until it is cleared, everyone is looking for a way round.

One overloaded junction can stop half a city. Perhaps it is time for a wider road.
ui.alert.story.strike:
A strike. The depot is shut, the trams are parked in a row and nobody is going anywhere. People are getting to work however they can.

While it lasts, the city has no transit at all. And happiness falls faster than takings.
ui.alert.story.riot:
Riots. Bins are burning in the streets, shop windows are broken and people are staying in. This did not fall out of the sky — it had been hanging in the air.

An unhappy city speaks up sooner or later. This is the later.
ui.alert.story.gangWar:
A gang war. There was shooting in the side streets; by morning there is a burnt-out car and nobody saw anything.

Where policing and work are missing, this moves in. The quarter will remember it for a long time.
ui.alert.story.blackout:
A blackout. The whole quarter is dark, lifts have stopped, fridges are thawing and nothing works in the shops.

The grid could not carry what was asked of it. Either add supply or cut demand — otherwise another one is coming.
ui.alert.story.epidemic:
An epidemic. Ambulances are queuing outside the hospital, a white tent has gone up on the lawn and people only go out when they must.

A city with few doctors and high density pays twice: first in health, then in mood.
ui.alert.story.chemicalSpill:
A chemical spill. An overturned tanker has emptied onto the road and from there into the drain. You can smell it three streets away.

The water here is unusable until it is cleaned up. And the works that draws from it will not deliver a drop.
ui.alert.story.landslide:
A landslide. The slope tore away and lay down across the road, together with the trees and a piece of the garden above it. Nothing gets through.

Hills look nice on the map. Cut into them and they occasionally answer back.
